title: DebianIssueReportV1
description:
The 1E.2 BTS snapshot report.

1E.2 RED: the struct is the *minimal* shape (`schema_version`, `report_kind`, `verdict`).

1E.2 GREEN: the struct gains the §23 comprehensive fields (`source_package`, `snapshot_at`, `bugs`, `summary`). The minimal shape is the JSON shape the 1E.1 `bts-helper.py` shim emits; the comprehensive shape is the same shape a 1E.2 consumer can read directly (the `bugs` list and `summary` are the §23 inventory of observed issues). Both shapes are RFC 8259 JSON; both carry the same `report_kind` discriminator and `verdict` tri-state; the comprehensive shape adds the observation fields.

The `verdict` is the §17 tri-state minus `Fail` (the BTS snapshot has no "fail" semantics per §24 — a snapshot either succeeded or the transport failed). The normalizer maps `verdict: pass` to `EvidenceStatus::Pass` and `verdict: infrastructure_error` to `NormalizationError::Unclassifiable(...)` per §24.

bugs.description: The list of bugs the BTS reported for `source_package`. Empty when the snapshot could not be retrieved.

snapshot_at.description: The RFC3339 UTC timestamp of when the snapshot was taken. Mirrors the 1E.1 shim's `snapshot_at` field. Empty when the snapshot could not be retrieved.

source_package.description: The source package name the snapshot was taken against. Mirrors the 1E.1 shim's `source_package` field. Empty when the snapshot could not be retrieved (`verdict: "infrastructure_error"`).

summary.description: The pre-computed summary fields. Mirrors the 1E.1 shim's `summary` field. `BugSummary::default()` when the snapshot could not be retrieved.

verdict.description: The §17 tri-state (minus `Fail` per §24). `pass` for a successful snapshot (regardless of how many bugs); `infrastructure_error` for any transport failure (DNS / TLS / timeout / SOAP / malformed service response).

BugRecord.description: A single bug record from the BTS snapshot. The shape matches the 1E.1 `bts-helper.py` output's `bugs[]` elements; downstream consumers (the agent, the exit artifact) read `id`, `severity`, `status`, and the `tags` list. The `forwarded` and `patch_tagged` booleans are derived from the `tags` list (the `bts-helper.py` does the derivation; the wire format exposes both the raw tags and the derived booleans so a consumer that reads only the wire format can answer §23 "is this bug patch-tagged? is it forwarded upstream?" without re-implementing the derivation).

forwarded.description: Derived flag: `true` iff the bug is `forwarded` upstream (the tag list contains `upstream` or `forwarded`). The 1E.1 shim computes this; the wire format exposes it so the §23 "forwarded upstream" question is answerable without re-deriving.

id.description: The BTS bug number. The BTS uses integers; the wire format keeps the integer type.

patch_tagged.description: Derived flag: `true` iff the bug has a patch attached (the tag list contains `patch`). The 1E.1 shim computes this; the wire format exposes it so the §23 "patch-tagged" question is answerable without re-deriving.

severity.description: The bug's severity as the BTS reports it. Common values: `critical`, `grave`, `serious`, `important`, `normal`, `minor`, `wishlist`. The wire format stores the raw string (the BTS does not constrain the set; new Debian releases can add severities without a wire-format change).

status.description: The bug's status as the BTS reports it. Common values: `open`, `done`, `forwarded`, `pending` (the BTS uses `pending-fixed`, `pending-upload`, etc.; the wire format stores the raw string).

subject.description: The bug's subject line. Stored verbatim from the BTS (the BTS does not enforce length; a §23 consumer can truncate for display).

tags.description: The bug's tags. The BTS exposes a free-form tag list (e.g. `patch`, `upstream`, `security`, `l10n`, `d-i`). The wire format stores the raw strings.

BugSummary.description:
The §23 summary fields. Computed from the `bugs` list by the 1E.1 shim; the wire format exposes the pre-computed values so a consumer that only reads the summary doesn't have to walk the bug list.

The §24 example output names all four fields: `open`, `serious`, `patch_tagged`, `forwarded`.

serious.description: Number of bugs with `status == "open"` AND `severity == "serious"` (or higher: `critical`, `grave`; the 1E.1 shim treats all of these as "serious" for the summary count).

IssueVerdict.description: The 1E.2 verdict tri-state. `Fail` is intentionally absent: §24 says the BTS snapshot has no `Fail` semantics — a snapshot either succeeded (the runtime observes the bug data) or the transport failed (the runtime gets `InfrastructureError → Blocked`). The `Pass` and `InfrastructureError` cases are the only two the 1E.2 normalizer distinguishes.

oneOf.description: The snapshot was retrieved successfully. The runtime records `EvidenceStatus::Pass`; the `bugs` list and `summary` (in the GREEN struct) carry the observation regardless of how many bugs there are — §24 "A package having 50 open bugs is not a tool failure."

The snapshot could not be retrieved (DNS / TLS / timeout / SOAP unavailable / malformed service response). The runtime records `NormalizationError::Unclassifiable(...)` which becomes `ExecutorError::InfrastructureFailed` which becomes `GateStatus::Blocked` (§24). The state-machine recovery path is 1F.1 / 1G.1's work.
